metadata.site_name: Gaick Lodge / Glen Tromie Basin, Cairngorms National Park

properties.description: High-angle oblique aerial perspective suspended 531m above the southern approach to Gaick Lodge, looking north-northeast into the glacial trough of Glen Tromie toward Loch Bhrodainn and Loch an t-Seilich.

properties.bedrock_formation: Grampian Group Dalradian Supergroup metasedimentary quartz-feldspar psammite and schist, intruded by Devonian granitic plutons
properties.glacial_geomorphology: Classic U-shaped glacial breach with steep scree talus slopes, lateral moraine deposits, and peat-veneered fluvioglacial gravels across the valley floor
properties.soil_taxonomy: Peaty podzols and dystric histosols (blanket bog) over compacted glacial till

properties.material: Unpaved highland estate track composed of crushed schorl/granite aggregate and compacted glacial gravel with central grassy berm
properties.topography: Gentle northward valley floor descent bordered by abrupt, scree-laden mountain flanks

properties.vegetation: Managed Calluna vulgaris heather moorland, degraded Molinia caerulea tussocks, and Eriophorum bog; symmetric planted shelterbelts of Pinus sylvestris (Scots pine) and Picea sitchensis bordering the lodge enclosure

properties.masonry: Locally quarried granite and whinstone rubble masonry, lime-harl coating, Ballachulish slate pitched roofing with lead flashing and stone chimneys
properties.layout: Enclosed walled compound with principal two-storey lodge and associated single-storey gabled keeper outbuildings and kennels
